title: wonder is now on stage at @A.R.T. until feb 15th!! what a magical adv...
transcript: I knew wonder was going to make me cry. I cried when I read the book, I cried when I watched the movie. Combine that with the fact that great big world is one of my favourite bands, and I knew it was going to get me. And yet still, I wasn't prepared. But it was a very easy call to drive up for the day to cambridge to check out the world premiere of wonder at american repertory theater. Wonder is about a seventh grade boy named auggie with facial differences. He's been homeschooled all his life, but now he's going to mainstream school for the first time. While auggie is definitely the lead, this is a show that is very much an ensemble piece. It plays with perspective shifts, going between auggie's point of view to his sister, to his friends. And I thought the entire cast was extremely strong. Storyline that made me cry. Them both was actually via, who is auggie's sister, played by caitlin hedges. Via loves her brother so much, but is also trying to find her own way and her own story. Maybe it's because i'm a big sister, but it just really got me. There are two boys that play auggie. We got to see garrett mcnally. I absolutely loved his performance, and they made a really interesting, creative choice that I really love of auggie's whole thing is he just wants to be ordinary. He has a facial difference that everybody Notices. When he meets people, he looks at the ground. At first, he doesn't wanna speak up or be seen or be photographed. So he has this imaginary astronaut best friend, played by nathan solstone, who does all of the singing for him. It's this really beautiful way of letting us inside auggie's world. And the moment where auggie is finally able to take ownership of his own voice sent me to literal outer space. I was completely undone. Now, wonder is a world premiere, and I think it is still trying to figure out who its audience exactly is. Sometimes it felt like it was for young children. Other times, middle schoolers or high schoolers and beyond. But I really loved it, and I think there's something very special here for everybody. I adored the music by great big world. I love the biography by katy spellman. Costuming and the set were incredibly detailed. The set kind of felt like you were in minecraft, which I thought was really brilliant. Since they're all building this world for auggie together. It's very imaginative and playful and important. Wonder is this beautiful story about kindness and perspective and learning to see the world differently. And i'm really glad it's being told at A R T. And it closes on february fifteenth, so if you get a chance, go and see it. I'm really glad I did.
